title: NeoMundi Evidence trust store, version 1
description: Public keys, identities and trust states used to verify Evidence attestations. PUBLIC MATERIAL ONLY -- a private key in this file would be a disclosure, and the verifier refuses a store containing a private-key field. The store lives OUTSIDE the Evidence repository: the repository ships only a test store under examples/, which grants nothing. Ne contient QUE du materiel public. Le magasin vit HORS du depot Evidence ; le depot n'embarque qu'un magasin de TEST, qui n'accorde rien.

store_id.description: Identifies this store. A verifier may be handed several; it never merges them silently.

store_kind.description: A `test` store exists for examples and tests. Keys in it grant nothing unless the verifier is explicitly run with --allow-test-keys.

verification_policy.description: THE POLICY IS EXPLICIT AND VERSIONED, not implied by code. A verifier states which policy it applied; a store that declares an unknown policy is refused rather than interpreted.

accepted_algorithms.description: The verifier IMPOSES the algorithm and never reads the JWS header to choose one. That is the defence against the algorithm-confusion family of attacks.

on_unknown_key.description: A key absent from the store yields NOT TESTED, never FAIL: the signature may be perfectly valid and we simply cannot know. Calling it invalid would be a groundless accusation.

on_rotated_key_within_window.description: Rotation means the key stopped being used. Signatures issued before the rotation stay trusted: nothing happened to the key.

on_compromised_key.description: Compromise invalidates EVERY signature by that key, whatever its declared date. Whoever holds the private key can forge any `attested_at_declared`, so letting earlier signatures survive would mean trusting a timestamp the attacker controls. This is the distinction with `rotated`, and the reason both are named separately.

identities.description: The identity registry. Entries are APPEND-ONLY and IMMUTABLE for the purposes of past attestations: an attestation binds to the identity ids as they stood when it was signed. A successor may be added later -- a commercial company succeeding an association, for instance -- and adding one NEVER invalidates earlier attestations. Identities are not revocable: revocation applies to KEYS. Whether an identity had the legal capacity to attest is a legal question, recorded here as a declaration and never decided by code.

kind.description: `machine` for a technical operator that is a host rather than a person. `unassigned` when a role exists but has not been attributed -- honest, and better than naming the wrong party.

registration_reference.description: A public registration reference, where one exists. Declared, never checked against a registry by this code.

legal_capacity_to_attest.description: DECLARED, never derived. The verifier reports this value and always returns NOT TESTED on legal capacity: no code can establish whether an entity may lawfully commit to an attestation. `not_applicable` for roles that commit to nothing, such as a technical operator.

superseded_by.description: Succession link. Adding it is additive: past attestations keep their verdict, and the verifier reports the succession without re-deciding anything.

keys.description: Public verification keys. A `kid` is never reused, and the verifier refuses a store with duplicate ids.

x.description: The raw 32-byte public key, base64url without padding. Same shape as RGC's `public_jwk()`, so one verification path serves both. It alone rebuilds the PEM, which is what makes the independent `openssl` check possible.

changes.description: Change history of this store, append-only. It is a record, not a proof: nothing here is independently timestamped.
